name: Avoid using signatures that are too weak to identify a file type on their own, except to confirm the type suggested by the extension
description: Short or generic header signatures, such as one or two bytes or common text, match many unrelated files. Using them alone to assign a type produces false identifications; restricting them to confirming the type suggested by the extension, or reporting them as weak, keeps the signature's evidential weight visible.

references.relevance_summary_280: Provides an implementation of this mitigation and is the origin of the term 'weak' used in this mitigation
